subject: 수능특강Light 영어
title: 영화에서 감정 전염을 일으키는 방식
fullPassage: Given the nature of emotional contagion, film is especially well suited to produce it. Carl Plantinga explains this in his discussion of the "scene of empathy," which refers to a scene in which the narrative slows down and a character's emotional experience becomes the focus of attention. Such scenes, which are typically shot in close-up and focus on a character's face, contain several eliciting conditions of emotional contagion. Actors' ability to accurately perceive and express genuine human emotions is also considered crucial in conveying emotional realism. Most important is attention, since contagion responses require that a spectator's attention be fixed on a character's facial expressions. Filmmakers achieve this through the use of extreme close-ups, shallow focus, and various point-of-view structures, and by using progressively closer shots of a character's face and expressions.
